02027d933cc0.src: with $p_{\mathrm{tr}} = 0.1\ \mathrm{MPa}$. Both limits follow from the denominator. When $|\Delta p| \ll p_{\mathrm{tr}}$, $(\Delta p^2 + p_{\mathrm{tr}}^2)^{1/4} \to p_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}$, so $g \to \Delta p/\sqrt{p_{\mathrm{tr}}}$: a straight line, like laminar flow. When $|\Delta p| \gg p_{\mathrm{tr}}$, $(\Delta p^2)^{1/4} = |\Delta p|^{1/2}$, so $g \to \Delta p/\sqrt{|\Delta p|} = \operatorname{sign}(\Delta p)\sqrt{|\Delta p|}$. At $\Delta p = p_{\mathrm{tr}}$ the two meet, and $g$ is $2^{-1/4} = 0.84$ of the pure square root. The function is smooth everywhere and handles reverse flow through the sign of $\Delta p$. It is a modelling choice, not a law of nature: it buys a well-behaved equation at the price of a small error in a range of pressure differences the press passes through quickly.

1df600921d63.src: That is the wave equation, and $c$ is the speed of sound in oil. (A rubber hose bulges as a wave passes and slows it somewhat, the Korteweg correction; the model ignores that.) A 2 m hose rings like an organ pipe at about $c/2L \approx 330\ \mathrm{Hz}$ and above. One rigid slug is a good model only well below that. The servo loop crosses over near 10 Hz (its loop gain falls through 1 there; chapter 18), so the lumped model is good where the controller works. The 174 Hz mode it predicts, the slug bouncing between the port volume and the cap chamber (worked solution 2 on the Servo-Hydraulic Press page evaluates it with the volumes of (12.1)), is however already halfway to the first wave mode, so treat its exact frequency with care.
1df600921d63.tr: وتلك هي معادلة الموجة، و$c$ سرعة الصوت في الزيت. 1e368359cd95.src: Apply the build-up equation (7.2) three times. The small volume at the valve port, $V_a$, which includes half the hose, receives $Q_A$ and sends $Q_h$ down the hose. The cap chamber receives $Q_h$ and grows as the ram rises. The rod chamber receives $Q_B$ and shrinks as the ram rises. The hose holds the volume $V_h = A_hL_h$; half of it is counted with each end. That split is the usual way to lump a line: the slug of chapter 11 carries the hose’s mass, and its compressibility, spread along its length, is shared between the two volumes it joins. Mind the case of the subscripts: $p_a$ is the pressure at the valve end of the hose, $p_A$ the pressure in the cap chamber at its far end.
1e368359cd95.tr: طبِّق معادلة بناء الضغط (7.2) ثلاث مرّات. فالحجم الصغير عند منفذ الصمّام، $V_a$، الذي يشمل نصف الخرطوم، يستقبل $Q_A$ ويرسل $Q_h$ عبر الخرطوم. وتستقبل الحجرة السفلى $Q_h$ وتكبر كلّما ارتفع المِدكّ. وتستقبل حجرة الساق $Q_B$ وتتقلّص كلّما ارتفع المِدكّ. ويحتوي الخرطوم على الحجم $V_h = A_hL_h$؛ ونحسب نصفه مع كلّ طرف. وهذا التقسيم هو الطريقة المعتادة لتجميع الخطّ في نقطة واحدة: فعمود الفصل 11 يحمل كتلة الخرطوم، وانضغاطيّته الموزّعة على طوله تُقسَم بين الحجمين اللذين يصلهما. وانتبه إلى الفرق بين الحرف الصغير والكبير في الأدلّة: $p_a$ ضغط عند طرف الخرطوم قرب الصمّام، و$p_A$ ضغط الحجرة السفلى عند طرفها البعيد.

539f49f92688.src: Equations (10.1), (12.1), (11.1) and (12.2), with the valve flows (9.1), friction (12.3) and contact (12.4), form a system $\dot{\mathbf{x}} = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}, u)$ of eight first-order nonlinear differential equations driven by one input, the command $u$. Every other quantity, the valve flows, the friction, the specimen force, is computed from the state at each instant: these are the dissipating blocks, the resistors, which store nothing. That is all the servo press is. The page integrates it with fourth-order Runge–Kutta at 100 steps per controller sample, and integrates seven more quantities alongside to keep the energy books (chapter 19).

5427012bcc27.src: Seal friction is not derived from first principles here, because nobody can: it depends on the rubber, the oil film and the surface finish. What can be explained is its shape. In 1902 Richard Stribeck measured the friction in lubricated bearings as a function of speed and found that it falls as speed rises from zero, reaches a minimum, and then grows again (Stribeck, Zeitschrift des Vereines deutscher Ingenieure 46, 1902). At rest and at crawling speed the seal touches the rod through a broken oil film, and solid friction dominates. As speed rises, the oil is dragged into the contact and lifts the seal off, so friction falls. At higher speed the film is complete and its viscous shear grows with speed.
5427012bcc27.tr: لا يُشتقّ احتكاك الحشوات هنا من المبادئ الأولى، لأنّ أحدًا لا يستطيع ذلك: فهو يعتمد على المطّاط، وعلى غشاء الزيت، وعلى نعومة السطح. ما يمكن تفسيره هو شكله. ففي عام 1902 قاس ريتشارد ستريبك الاحتكاك في المحامل المزيّتة بدلالة السرعة، فوجد أنّه ينخفض مع ارتفاع السرعة من الصفر، ويبلغ حدًّا أدنى، ثم يعاود الازدياد (ستريبك، Zeitschrift des Vereines deutscher Ingenieure 46، 1902). وعند السكون وعند السرعة الزاحفة تلامس الحشوةُ الساقَ عبر غشاء زيت متقطّع، فيسود الاحتكاك الجاف. ومع ارتفاع السرعة يُسحب الزيت إلى نقطة التلامس فيرفع الحشوةَ عنها، فينخفض الاحتكاك. وعند سرعة أعلى يكتمل الغشاء، فيزداد قصّه اللزج مع السرعة.

7adbf054bd65.src: Whether the flow stays laminar depends on the Reynolds number $Re = \bar{u}\,d/\nu$, the ratio of inertial to viscous forces. Above about 2300 the flow becomes turbulent. Eddies then carry momentum across the pipe far more effectively than viscosity does, and the wall stress no longer depends on the viscosity but on the density and the speed. Dimensional analysis then fixes the form: the only pressure that can be built from $\rho$ and $\bar{u}$ is $\tfrac12\rho\bar{u}^2$, and the drop must grow in proportion to the length per diameter, $L/d$. The dimensionless factor in front, the friction factor $f$, is measured. Adding the losses in fittings and bends, $K_m$, gives the Darcy–Weisbach law:
7adbf054bd65.tr: يتوقّف بقاء الجريان طبقيًّا على عدد رينولدز $Re = \bar{u}\,d/\nu$، وهو نسبة قوى القصور إلى قوى اللزوجة. وفوق نحو 2300 يصير الجريان مضطربًا. عندئذٍ تنقل الدوّامات كمّية الحركة عبر الأنبوب بكفاءة أكبر بكثير من اللزوجة، ولا يعود إجهاد الجدار يتعلّق باللزوجة، بل بالكثافة والسرعة. ثم يحدّد تحليلُ الأبعاد الصيغةَ: فالضغط الوحيد الذي يمكن تكوينه من $\rho$ و$\bar{u}$ هو $\tfrac12\rho\bar{u}^2$، ويجب أن يزداد الهبوط بنسبة طول الأنبوب إلى قطره $L/d$. أمّا العامل عديم البُعد الذي أمامه، أي معامل الاحتكاك $f$، فيُقاس تجريبيًّا. وبإضافة خسائر الوصلات والانحناءات $K_m$ نحصل على قانون دارسي–وايسباخ:

ba467fe47408.src: The specimen is a spring $k_w$ with a damper $c_w$ in parallel (a Kelvin–Voigt solid); the damper is set to 5 % of critical. Critical damping is the value that separates bouncing from creeping: for a mass $m$ on a spring $k$ with damper $c$, the motion $m\ddot{\delta} + c\dot{\delta} + k\delta = 0$ goes as $e^{\lambda t}$ with $m\lambda^2 + c\lambda + k = 0$, whose roots are real, so the motion does not oscillate, once $c^2 \ge 4mk$. The boundary is $c_{\mathrm{crit}} = 2\sqrt{km}$, and here $c_w = 0.05\cdot 2\sqrt{k_w m}$, with $m = 160\ \mathrm{kg}$ the ram that presses on the specimen: a lightly damped specimen, as a steel part is. It is only touched when the platen has climbed past $y_c$, and it can push but not pull:

ecafdb0f7e07.src: At $\omega = \omega_v$ the real part of the denominator vanishes and the response is $1/(2j\zeta_v)$: the spool lags by exactly 90°, whatever the damping. That is how $f_v$ is measured. Here $\operatorname{atan2}(b, a)$ is the angle of the complex number $a + jb$, so the phase runs smoothly from 0 through −90° at $\omega_v$ towards −180°. The plain form $\varphi = -\arctan(b/a)$ would be wrong above resonance, where $a < 0$: at 100 Hz it gives +52.7° instead of −127.3°.
